title: Defined Benefit vs Defined Contribution (Exam Favorite)

blocks.content: Under Defined Benefit schemes, the employer bears the investment risk, whereas under Defined Contribution schemes, the risk is shifted to the employee.

items: National Pension System (NPS) is a Defined Contribution (DC) scheme implemented for central government recruits starting January 1, 2004.
Old Pension Scheme (OPS) is an unfunded Defined Benefit (DB) scheme funded out of current government revenues.
Exams often test who bears the investment risk: Employer in DB vs Employee in DC.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Defined Benefit (DB) schemes promise a predefined pension payout calculated using salary history and service length.
Defined Contribution (DC) schemes fix the contribution amount, while final retirement payout depends entirely on market returns.
In Defined Benefit plans, financial and investment risk is entirely borne by the employer or government.
In Defined Contribution plans, individual subscribers bear all market investment risks.
Central Government of India transitioned from DB (Old Pension Scheme) to DC (National Pension System) for employees joining on or after January 1, 2004.
